X.note: Strong, believable ruined walls and raking light. The soldiers are small, uniformly lit, saturated and doll-like, packed into a tight clump with the same pose repeated. The left group is more varied and legible, with a drummer and an officer. The Union flag is tiny, and at this size the design can't be checked. The scale of the people against the buildings is slightly off.

Y.note: Same set and lighting as X. The left-hand figures are fewer and one has a smeared green-black face and torso, so it reads as a glitch. The figures look more like flat game-asset cutouts, with weaker silhouettes and a thinner crowd. An added barrel on the right is a small plus. The Union flag is the same tiny, unverifiable one.

why: The environments are identical, but X's foreground soldiers are more varied and coherent, while Y has a malformed figure and a thinner, more toy-like group.
top_fix_for_weaker: Redo the foreground soldiers: remove or regenerate the smeared green-faced figure, vary poses and spacing, and give them real shadows, contact grounding and scale-correct detail. Add smoke, dust or rubble interaction so they stop reading as pasted figures.
anachronisms_seen: Union flag too small to verify; the post-1801 design with the St Patrick's saltire would be wrong for 1782
Uniform colours are uniformly saturated and clean for a besieged garrison
Shutters and windows are mostly intact despite the bombardment-ruined walls
